comparator.name: Criminology
comparator.sourceNotes: The current2026–2027 BA-CRIM programme introduces the revised curriculum by cohort from September2025: years1 and2 each contain twelve compulsory5EC modules, independently confirmed in all24current module responses. These120EC are retained. Its displayed year3 explicitly belongs to entrants2024 or earlier, and the revised year3 will be included in the2027–2028 guide. The outgoing35EC required,15elective and10thesis table is not attached to the revised first120. Current prospective overview now describes a third-year minor followed by three thematic units and a thesis, but supplies no complete weights/named-unit/entry framework. The detailed structure page still describes15EC curricular electives and a30EC extracurricular minor. This discrepancy replaces the earlier assumption that all current pages agreed on15EC. No minor or thesis credits are inferred. The Dutch criminological language test and LLP tutoring/practice programme are zero-credit first-year obligations; their meetings and language test are related parts, not additional EC. The separate aggregate LLP endpoint is null and is not counted as another activity. Quantitative Research1 supplies preparation for2, and both precede Experiments. Qualitative2 description includes a circular self-reference, but its admission text requires regular Criminology enrolment, not completion of itself. Introduction to Criminal Law is explicitly required in BA-CRIM but its module admission prose only lists regular Law and Criminology minor students; eligibility for the ordinary Criminology student needs clarification before full pathway certification. No external curriculum or UCR correspondence is certified as complete.

audience.programmeDescription: Criminology at Leiden studies crime, its causes and consequences, and the ways society responds to it. The programme combines legal, psychological and sociological perspectives with qualitative, quantitative and experimental research. Students examine offenders, victims, prevention, policing and criminal justice.
audience.comparisonExplanation: A complete UCR comparison is not yet available because the revised third-year curriculum has not been established from the available official information. The confirmed first two years are shown below. This incomplete external curriculum does not establish that UCR offers no suitable study possibilities.

curriculum.limitation: These 24 compulsory courses total 120 EC, covering the first two years. The remaining 60 EC, including the third-year choices and thesis, require confirmation for the revised curriculum. First-year tutoring and a Dutch criminological language test are additional zero-credit obligations. This is an incomplete curriculum, not a certified 180-EC degree plan.

componentNotes.y1-criminal-law: This course is listed as compulsory in the programme. Its admission wording needs clarification for regular Criminology students.
componentNotes.y2-quantitative-research-2: Builds on Quantitative Criminological Research 1; successful completion of that course is recommended before participation.
componentNotes.y2-qualitative-research-2: Develops qualitative analysis of secondary data and coding. The first-year research courses provide the preparatory foundation.
